newsitem.title: USA: U.S., North Korea continue New York talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S., North Korea continue New York talks.

text.p: North Korea and the United States on Monday continued talks in New York on joint efforts to account for 8,100 U.S. troops still listed as missing from the 1950-53 Korean War, the Pentagon said.
The U.S. Defence Department said the discussions, which began on Sunday, were taking place at an undisclosed location and were expected to last through at least Thursday.
"The first round wound up on Sunday night with an agreement to continue," said Air Force Lt. Col. Joan Ferguson, a Pentagon spokeswoman.

U.S.-North Korean talks on missing troops were last held in May 1996. They led to an agreement which resulted in joint recovery of the remains of a American Army corporal, but were derailed when a North Korean submarine loaded with commandos ran aground last September off South Korea.

The United States paid North Korea $2 million to cover the cost of last year's search operation but has asked Pyongyang to stop returning remains of suspected U.S. troops until further joint searches can be set up in order to make identifications easier.

The Pentagon announced last week that the new round of talks would also deal with U.S. questions about reports of Americans possibly living in North Korea. Washington wants access to North Korean files on Americans held prisoner in the North during the war.
Ferguson said one topic of the negotiations includes a possible schedule for resuming joint excavations at sites believed to contain remains of U.S. servicemen buried or shot down during the war.

The latest talks are separate from negotiations that broke off last month in New York in which the United States and South Korea urged Pyongyang to begin four-way peace talks with China to negotiate a formal end to the Korean War.
